title: Scene properties that reference external subresources modify their paths and make the internal subresources on save.
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced in 4.71 and 4.8 latest

### System information

Windows 11 and Mac OS X and Kubuntu

### Issue description

When saving a scene, external subreferences are not respected as external references, but have their paths modified and are made internal. Not just duplicates, the original owning resources now point to the saved scene. 
The problem seems to be because ```ResourceFormatSaverTextInstance::_find_resources``` checks ```res->is_built_in()``` , which will always be true for subresource paths(any path with "::" is seen as built in)
The resource saver assumes the level owns this resource and modifies it's path and saves it inside the scene file.
These resources should be marked as external as they have a valid path outside the scene.

My intention was to bundle several generated textures and materials from asset imports into subresources to avoid clutter, but textures and materials need to be assigned to exported properties to render in most nodes, triggering this issue. The workaround is to not use subresources and to export each asset as it's own resource.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a custom resource with a subresource texture, generate a 1x1 ImageTexture in code. attach your custom resource to a Sprite2D property, in that node's code get the subresource and assign it to Sprite2D's texture.
The subresource will have the correct path until you save the scene.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[texture-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32675530/texture-test.zip)
